answer: A market beside a river keeps its ledger honest by treating every trader like a sparrow that must sing a different song at each surprise inspection. Every identity faces random audits drawn by lottery from established peers, and the load grows with each identity its operator holds: the first answers 1 audit per cycle, the tenth answers 10, each demanding a fresh, non-reusable proof of distinct work. A farmer running fakes in parallel cannot pass, because audits arrive unpredictably and no proof can be copied across identities, just as no two opals share the same flash.
